parts.text:
A security code consists of one letter chosen from $\{A,\; B,\; C,\; D\}$ followed by one digit chosen from $\{1,\; 2,\; 3,\; 4,\; 5\}$.
Calculate the total number of possible codes, and explain why multiplication is used.

questions.title: Arranging Distinct People in a Straight Line

parts.text:
Six people stand in a straight line for a photograph.
Calculate the number of different possible arrangements, expressing your method in terms of a factorial.

Eight runners compete in a final. Gold, silver, and bronze medals are awarded to the first three finishers.
Calculate the number of different possible podium outcomes, and state why order matters.

Six different bicycles are to be parked in $10$ numbered parking spaces in a row.
Calculate the number of different possible parking arrangements.

questions.title: Permutations of Repeated Letters in LEVEL

parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of all $5$ letters in the word LEVEL.

questions.title: Permutations of Repeated Letters in BALLOONS

parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of all $8$ letters in the word BALLOONS.

A car park has $15$ parking spaces in a single row. Four different cars are parked in four of these spaces.
Calculate the number of possible parking arrangements.

Two particular spaces at the ends of the row are reserved for electric vehicles. If two of the four cars are electric vehicles that must occupy these two reserved spaces, calculate the number of possible parking arrangements for all four cars.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $9$ letters in the word SUCCESSOR.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $9$ letters in SUCCESSOR that begin with the letter U and end with the letter R.

questions.title: Permutations of RELEASED with End Restrictions

parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of all $8$ letters in the word RELEASED.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $8$ letters in RELEASED that start and end with the letter E.

questions.title: Permutations of CELESTIAL with Initial and Final Restrictions

parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of all $9$ letters in the word CELESTIAL.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $9$ letters in CELESTIAL that begin with the letter C and end with the letter T.

questions.title: Hall Seating Arrangements and Row Restrictions

parts.text:
A village hall has $40$ distinct seats arranged in $8$ rows of $5$ seats each. Five people enter the hall.
Calculate the number of possible seating arrangements if there are no restrictions on where the people sit.
Find the number of possible seating arrangements if all five people must sit in the front row of $5$ seats.

questions.title: Seating Eight Students in Labelled Rows with Named Constraints

parts.text:
Eight different students sit in two labelled rows, Row $A$ and Row $B$, each having four seats in a line.
Calculate the total number of seating arrangements if there are no restrictions on where the students sit.

Two of the students, Lina and Omar, must both sit in Row $A$.
Find the number of seating arrangements that satisfy this condition.
Find the number of seating arrangements in which Lina must sit in Row $A$ and Omar must sit in Row $B$.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $11$ letters in the word MATHEMATICS.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $11$ letters in MATHEMATICS that start and end with the letter M.
Find the number of different arrangements of all $11$ letters in MATHEMATICS in which the four vowels (A, E, A, I) are all next to each other.
